justification: LLM extraction became the default on 2026-09-21, and AI_MODEL defaulted to a provider whose key is not set in this environment, reading it with a bare os.environ[...]. Every chapter extraction now takes that path, so the default configuration raised KeyError before reading a page.

pre_impl.existing_data: No database, no schema, no network in the change itself. The only inputs are environment variables and the existing _PROVIDERS mapping, which is unchanged.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: Turning AI_EXTRACTION on by default was treated as a one-line switch. It was not: it moved a previously opt-in code path onto every extraction, and that path had an unguarded os.environ['MISTRAL_API_KEY'] behind a default of AI_MODEL='mistral'. Measured in this environment: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, OPENAI_API_KEY and GEMINI_API_KEY are set and MISTRAL_API_KEY is not. The module docstring also still read 'Enabled by AI_EXTRACTION=1; off by default', which the same change had made false.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: No new provider and no new mechanism. _PROVIDERS already maps four models to their call functions; this adds a preference list over the same names and a helper that returns the first whose key is present. The explicit AI_MODEL setting is still consulted first and still wins.
pre_impl.external_source_error: This is the code that chooses which paid API to call. A missing key now fails before any request with a message naming every key it looked for. A key that is present but unusable -- the Anthropic account was out of credit when this was found -- is a different failure and still surfaces as the provider's own error, loudly, from _call_with_retry. Deliberately not papered over: a credit problem is not a configuration problem and should not be silently routed around.
pre_impl.frontend_type: No API, component or type change.
pre_impl.user_failure_mode: Two directions. Defaulting to an unconfigured provider makes every extraction fail on a KeyError that names one variable and explains nothing -- the same shape as the data-watch job that died on os.environ['PGHOST'] the same night and blocked every merge for three days. Silently falling back to any provider that answers would be worse: the models are not interchangeable, haiku made a real-chapter error which is why sonnet was added, and a chapter read by a model nobody chose is a result nobody can reason about. So the choice is deterministic, ordered by evidence, and stated.

falsifiable_check.fails_when: the default reverts to a fixed model name; a blank or whitespace-only key counts as configured; the no-key case returns a guess instead of raising; the preference order stops putting the hand-verified model first; an explicit AI_MODEL stops overriding the default; the error message stops naming every key it looked for or the AI_EXTRACTION=0 escape; a preference entry names a model that is not in _PROVIDERS; or the module docstring goes back to claiming the extractor is off by default.
falsifiable_check.observed_red: 5 mutations planted, 5 caught: default reverted to a fixed model, blank key treated as configured, no-key case returning 'mistral' instead of raising, preference order flipped to put mistral first, and the stale docstring restored. 12 tests here.

functions.name: _default_model
functions.input: No arguments; reads the provider key environment variables named in _MODEL_PREFERENCE.
functions.output: The name of the first model whose key is present and non-blank, or RuntimeError naming every key it looked for.
functions.if_none: No provider key at all raises rather than guessing. That is correct and must stay: extraction is now the default path, so a silent fallback would read a whole council's plan with a model nobody selected.

functions.name: _MODEL_PREFERENCE
functions.input: A declared ordering of (model name, env key) pairs.
functions.output: The order _default_model walks. Ordered by evidence of working on a real chapter, not by price.
functions.if_none: An empty list would make _default_model always raise, which a test would catch via the provider-name check.

values.name: sonnet is preferred over mistral
values.why: Not a price ranking. sonnet was hand-verified on marrickville/part7-s3-sex-industry -- 49 of 49 objectives and controls, every section number correct -- and was added on 2026-09-05 specifically because haiku made a real-chapter error. mistral is the cheapest and was the old default, but it answered 429 on both attempts ever made with it, and its key is absent here.
values.source: project-ai-extraction-decided-but-unused-2026-09 and the module's own validation notes.
values.if_missing: The default picks whichever provider is alphabetically or accidentally first, and a council's plan is read by a model chosen by nothing.

values.name: a blank key is not a configured key
values.value: (os.getenv(k) or '').strip() rather than k in os.environ
values.why: Setting a variable to an empty string is how a deployment records one it has not filled in yet. Treating that as configured selects a provider that will fail on its first call, after the download and the chunking.
values.source: Standard deployment behaviour; pinned by a test because the membership test reads as equivalent.
values.if_missing: A half-provisioned environment fails late and expensively instead of immediately.

queries.purpose: None. This change reads environment variables only and issues no SQL.

break_it.scenario: A provider key is present but the account cannot be used.
break_it.what_happens: Exactly what happened when this was found: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY was set and the API answered 'Your credit balance is too low'. The run failed, wrote nothing, and left needs_extraction=TRUE for retry.
break_it.how: Deliberately not handled here. A credit or quota problem is not a configuration problem, and routing around it silently would pick a different model for one chapter and not the next -- which is exactly the non-determinism the proof gate exists to bound. It surfaces as the provider's own error from _call_with_retry, loudly.

break_it.scenario: Someone adds a provider to _PROVIDERS but not to _MODEL_PREFERENCE.
break_it.what_happens: It is never chosen by default, however well configured. Not an error, but a capability that quietly does nothing -- the same shape as the extractor that sat off for two months.
break_it.how: Not caught. The test asserts the reverse direction, that every preference entry names a real provider, because a typo there silently skips a configured provider and falls through to one that is not.

break_it.scenario: The preference order is treated as a cost ranking and re-sorted.
break_it.what_happens: mistral returns to the front on price and the default becomes a model that has answered 429 on every attempt, in an environment with no key for it.
break_it.how: The ordering carries its reasoning inline, and a test pins sonnet ahead of mistral when both keys are present.

break_it.scenario: No provider key at all, and the change guesses one anyway.
break_it.what_happens: The chapter is read by a model nobody selected and the failure appears later as a provider auth error, after the PDF download and chunking, attributed to the wrong thing.
break_it.how: It raises, naming every key it looked for and the AI_EXTRACTION=0 escape. A planted mutation that returns 'mistral' instead is caught.

break_it.scenario: The docstring keeps saying the extractor is off by default.
break_it.what_happens: The next reader believes a switch is opt-in when it is the default, which is how it was left off for two months after being verified.
break_it.how: Corrected, and a test asserts the old wording cannot come back.

post_merge.secrets: No. It reads the presence of provider key variables and never prints, logs or transmits their values.
post_merge.manual_verify: Confirm the Railway dcp-extract service has at least one provider key set, since extraction is now the default path there; without one every nightly run will now raise this error by design rather than silently reading with the regex reader.
